title: Veneer, crown, bridge: what each one is
intro: Every plan is written with these words. Here is what each piece does, so your estimate reads like plain English.

items.d: A thin porcelain shell bonded to the front of a tooth to change its color, shape and length. Only about 0.3 mm of the tooth is prepared, so it stays almost intact.
items.alt: Illustration of a thin porcelain veneer being placed on the front of a tooth

items.d: A porcelain cap that covers the whole tooth. For teeth that are broken, heavily filled or root-canaled and need strength as well as looks.
items.alt: Illustration of a full porcelain crown about to seat over a prepared molar

items.d: A partial crown that covers three of the tooth's four walls and leaves the healthy side untouched. Less tooth reduction than a full crown.
items.alt: Illustration of a three-quarter crown covering three walls of a premolar

items.d: One or more replacement teeth held by crowns on the neighbouring teeth. Closes a gap without surgery.
items.alt: Illustration of a three-unit dental bridge over a missing tooth

items.d: A titanium post placed in the bone with a porcelain crown on top. Replaces a missing tooth, root and all.
items.alt: Illustration of a dental implant post in the bone with a crown on top

items.d: A full row of fixed teeth on four to six implants per jaw. Replaces every tooth in the arch at once.
items.alt: Illustration of a full arch of fixed teeth on four implants
